subject: Next steps: private onramp & SDK auth options for SomaHealth
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@somahealth.io>, Claire Liu <claire.liu@somahealth.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: private onramp & SDK auth options for SomaHealth

Hi Rajiv / Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + suggested path forward so we have a single checklist for your networking and auth teams. High level: SomaHealth wants a private integration for PHI workloads with predictable latency and a gradual rollout (dev -> staging -> prod). The items below cover SDK setup, auth choices, routing, structured output/tool-calling, embeddings/rerank, and the networking pieces we discussed.

Action items we promised:
- Redwood to propose recommended auth patterns for dev vs prod (API key, mTLS, private VPC endpoint).
- Provide a VPC endpoint checklist (CIDR/IPs, DNS, egress rules, NAT).
- Confirm structured-output support (tool calling + schema enforcement) and how to bind it to your backend endpoints.
- Share a starter SDK quickstart and embedding/reranker guidance for your search team.

Technical asks for SomaHealth (please send by Tue):
1) Network: expected egress CIDR(s) or whether you want Redwood to host a VPC endpoint in your account (AWS/GCP) vs using our managed private link.
2) Security: does the security team require mutual TLS (mTLS) for all prod traffic, or will a KMS-backed API key + IP allowlist be acceptable initially?
3) Traffic profile: expected sustained QPS and burst during peak (helps sizing).
4) Integration owner(s): who on your infra team will own firewall/NAT changes and who on app side owns SDK rollout?

What we'll deliver:
- A short VPC endpoint checklist (attached) and a reference network diagram.
- SDK quickstart (attached) with examples for structured output + tool calling hooks you can plug to your services.
- Design recommendation on embeddings + reranker (latency vs cost trade-offs).

Next steps / timeline:
- You provide answers to the 4 technical asks above (by Tue).
- We schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your networking and security teams (Thursday preferred).
- Post-deep-dive: we provide a tailored onramp plan and a canary test window.

Attachments: redwood_private_connectivity_checklist.pdf, rdw-sdk-quickstart.md

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@somahealth.io>

Cc: Claire Liu <claire.liu@somahealth.io>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: private onramp & SDK auth options for SomaHealth

Ben — thanks for the clear notes. Claire and I captured the items and looped in our network/security leads (netsupport@somahealth.io). A few clarifications and answers inline: 

Network answers:
- We prefer a private VPC endpoint hosted in our AWS account (VPC peering/VPC endpoint service) rather than routing through a public IP allowlist. I'll share a network diagram (attached) and can provide a read-only role if you need to validate routing.
- Egress: our environment egresses through a managed NAT; we will need Redwood's list of outbound IPs if you require IP allowlisting for other destinations (e.g., model telemetry endpoints).

Security / auth:
- For prod handling PHI, our security policy requires mTLS with certs from our internal PKI. For non-PHI dev/staging we can use scoped API keys.
- We also need a SOC2 attestation and an explanation of data retention for logs that might include user prompts.

Traffic:
- Initial pilot: ~10 QPS steady, 100 QPS burst for short periods. If we roll broader, we expect 200–500 QPS.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can your SDK perform automatic connection reuse over a VPC endpoint and surface structured-output validation errors to our service?
2) For embeddings: do you have a recommended pipeline for storing vectors and running a cheap reranker in our VPC to avoid crossing public boundaries?

Attached: soma_network_diagram.png (diagram)

Regards,
Rajiv Menon
CTO, SomaHealth
rajiv.menon@somahealth.io

Rajiv / team —

Thanks for the diagram and the traffic numbers. A few concrete recommendations from engineering to make the onramp predictable and minimize coordination:

1) VPC endpoint approach (recommended):
- We can stand up a PrivateLink / Private Service in your AWS account. That gives you full control over routing and mTLS termination inside your network. Redwood will run a lightweight agent in our managed plane to accept traffic, but the endpoint is hosted by you.
- Requirements from your side: destination CIDR for the endpoint, the VPC ID, and a role for validation. We can provide CloudFormation/Terraform snippets.

2) Auth: staged approach
- Dev/Staging: scoped API keys rotated via our Console + IP allowlist for CI runners.
- Prod (PHI): mTLS with your internal PKI. Redwood supports client-side cert verification; you'll need to provide CA bundle or let us validate against your ACME PKI. We also support KMS-backed HSM keys if you need to sign request metadata.

3) DNS & egress
- We'll publish a customer-specific internal DNS name per environment (e.g., rdw.prod.soma.internal) that resolves to the VPC endpoint. If you prefer to manage DNS, we can give the A/ALIAS records.
- Egress from your VPC to any external telemetry endpoints can be limited; if you want zero public egress we recommend running our optional telemetry relay in your VPC (small lambda/container) so logs never leave your account.

4) SDK + structured output/tool-calling
- Our SDK supports structured-output schemas and will return schema validation errors in-band. You can configure the SDK to enforce strict decoding (fail fast) or return best-effort + error payloads for offline reconciliation.
- For tool calling, the SDK can emit a signed webhook to your internal service over mTLS, or call via a private function URL bound into the VPC endpoint. Both support idempotency keys and callback verification.

5) Embeddings + rerankers
- Option A (recommended): host vector DB in your VPC (e.g., Milvus/FAISS on EC2/RDS) and call Redwood embeddings over the private link. Store vectors locally and run a lightweight reranker in VPC to avoid returning raw embeddings off-site.
- Option B: use Redwood embeddings with an encrypted store we manage; we can provide a zero-data-retention SLA for matching workloads.

Checklist questions for your network team (quick):
- Provide VPC ID, subnet IDs for endpoint, and an account role for validation.
- Confirm whether your PKI team can issue a client cert or share a CA bundle.
- Will you allow our validation role to provision an endpoint service?

If helpful I can drop a reference Terraform/CF template and a small runbook for the security review. Also attaching the SDK quickstart and the network checklist Ben mentioned.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Rajiv / Claire —

Appreciate the quick replies and the diagram. Short summary of agreed next steps and owners: 

1) Networking: SomaHealth netsupport will share VPC ID, subnets, and a validation role by Wed EOD (owner: netsupport@somahealth.io). Redwood (Karthik) will prepare Terraform snippets and a PrivateLink onboarding doc (owner: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai).
2) Auth: Security will require mTLS for prod. Action: SomaHealth PKI to provide CA bundle or issue a client cert (owner: SomaHealth PKI). For dev/staging we’ll use scoped API keys (owner: Ben / Claire to manage access).
3) Embeddings/rerank: We recommend hosting vector DB in your VPC for PHI. Karthik will send a short pros/cons note and an example pipeline (owner: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai).
4) Scheduling: Tech deep-dive — Thu May 20, 2027 at 11:00 AM PT. I'll send the invite; please add the engineers who will own VPC and PKI.

Open questions that we should cover in the deep-dive:
- Exact CIDR and whether you want the endpoint inside a private subnet only.
- Whether netsupport wants an audit-only mode for telemetry or zero-copy relay.
- Any compliance paperwork (SOC2) we should attach to the invite for your security reviewers.

I'll create a shared Slack channel and drop all artifacts there after the invite goes out. Thanks — feel free to reply with any add-ons.

Ben Carter
